title: Head of the class and the Constitution newspaper visit
summary: Newspaper people visit his class; Green talks about the records shop and Tom Bailey's theatre.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: So I finally went up to -- like I was saying, they come up to this school, and whoever was in the head of the class, they would always get chosen to do something, some kind of chore that would be helpful to them in their education.

So one day there some newspaper people from a very popular newspaper in that city was called The Constitution. They were there, some, you know, some publisher, editor, like that. And I would always happen to be in the head of the class, --
-- with these compositions, and you know, you'd have to stand up, and you say a few things about your composition.
It was almost like a philosopher or something, you
It was like a show and tell?

Yeah, well, you see, in this school in that grade, you see, by that time I was in the third grade. You understand? So (clapping rhythms) may I be excused now, please, because I -- could you because --
Okay, I guess you're -- you're back now, Chuck, and what were you saying?

Well, I was speaking about that grade. I was in the third grade. And I had acquired a way of talking similar to the late-great Bert Williams, who was in a famous team of Williams and Walker. And that's why -- I guess it's some kind of comical way of speaking, you see, and as I say, I go along with the story about this daughter-in-law of the fight promoter, Mr. George Ruby.
Well, she had the record shop . I think I said that before -- next to Mr. Tom Bailey's theater, which was where Brown Skinned Buddies, Brown Skinned Models --
